item.description:
Desktop widgets can now read AI usage snapshots in ad-hoc builds without requiring a paid Apple Developer account or a provisioned App Group.
- Keep App Group storage as the first choice for configured team builds; fall back to an owner-only Application Support directory for ad-hoc builds. - Grant the sandboxed widget read-only access to that snapshot directory. API keys and OAuth tokens are never written to the widget snapshot. - Save provider-page and 30-day chart-metric selections in widget-local preferences without an App Group. - Keep the last snapshot available after the app quits. Refreshing provider data requires the app to be running. - Set the app and extension marketing version to 0.1.1 and document the fallback.
Validation: Xcode build; 98 Swift tests; 48 release-script tests; universal arm64/x86_64 archive and ad-hoc signature verification. On macOS 27.2.1, the installed extension generated medium and large timelines. A separate sandboxed probe using production code verified real snapshot reads, denied writes, paging and metric persistence across processes, refresh notification delivery, and reads after the app quit.
Desktop visual rendering and button delivery through chronod remain unverified because the test session lacked Accessibility and screen capture access. The sandboxed probe checks do not replace those UI checks. Compatibility and upgrade behavior may vary by macOS version.
The app is not notarized by Apple. After installing in Applications and trying to launch it, macOS may require System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
Thanks to TheBoredTeam and boringNotch contributors for the original app and architecture, and to lyrimuse, lycrics_notch, MediaRemoteAdapter, and the other projects credited in the README and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.
